what_was_done: The orchestrating session recorded the sanction: rewrite/plans/step-4/ORDER.md section 4 has a verdicts row for story_unit.py (acs is the one reader of acceptance criteria, skips code fences, verdicts._story_acs delegates to it), and the launch notes of survey-2, which rewrites that file, say that acs is kept as it is.

The orchestrating session corrected the module docstring of gate_evidence.py: the review lookup is what vsdd.state.verdicts.covering answers (the computed verdict when it covers the head, else the closure's stored verdict). A comment only; no behaviour changed.

Not on the slice path: it needs a clone, or a machine that lost its local records, whose closure already carries a round count, and the slice is one run on one machine with records kept. For M3 (hand-off between clones) with S3 and G3: the survey records, on the run record, the rounds_used it hands the script for each story; verdicts._rebuild replays each run's loop 1 with that recorded figure, using rule 9's count only for a run without it; rounds_used() is the recorded figure plus the run's own passes. Correct the comment in _rebuild that says a clone with short records follows the closure's stored verdict, and add the test_verdicts case of the finding's probe (closure rounds_used 1, cap 3, no earlier records, a dispute ruled not_defect) expecting converged/clean and a covering() answer.

For G3 when the conformance cases are next extended (with G6a's holdout cases at the latest): add one records case whose stored passes continue after a blocked review, the following pass's review receiving the rebuilt claims, so that the continue rule is pinned as the walk-on-after-clean rule is by r20.

For B6 with S2a, when a workflow beyond the shipped story script is built (W3 first): lint the step-name grammar the verdict relies on (review-<lens>-l<n>-p<k>, fix-<agent>-l<n>-p<k>, arbitrate-l<n>) in every workflow script, so that one record per pass cannot be overwritten under a shared name; the story script's scenario tests already assert its names.
